title: Cans — choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Channel Strip for the Cans menu-bar popover. Keep it, take an alternate, steer, or re-roll. Tell me in steer if anything must stay (e.g. dark only, the headphone photo).

options.label: Channel Strip
options.lineage: Analog mixing-console channel strips (SSL / Neve / Mackie)
options.thesis: Your headphones as one live channel on a desk: mode is the input switch, ambient is the fader.
options.viewport: A single vertical strip: scribble strip with name, codec and battery ladder on top; lit Off / NC / Ambient push-buttons; a long ambient fader with 20 detents and Focus on Voice as a latch; EQ as six mini faders; deeper settings slide in as an insert rack.
options.risk: Turns into costume skeuomorphism if bevels, screws or fake metal creep in; it has to stay flat, crisp and native.

raised.raise: One level ramp everywhere: battery, ambient, volume and pressure all read as the same segmented LED ladder, never mixed gauges.
State is a mark, not just a hue: every lit button also changes its legend and shape, so colour is never the only signal.
One colour by law: signal green means a live control link and nothing else; amber is the only accent for 'on'.

options.label: Front Panel
options.thesis: A brushed-aluminium amplifier faceplate: a detented selector knob, one amber meter, engraved legends.
options.viewport: A faceplate popover: rotary selector for Off / NC / Ambient, an amber needle meter for ambient level, engraved labels, settings behind a hinged lower panel.
options.risk: The most familiar audiophile move, and light aluminium clashes with a dark menu bar.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: Theatre lighting: a cyclorama passing from night to day
options.thesis: Noise control as light: NC is night, Ambient is day, and the horizon band shows how much of the world you let in.
options.viewport: The popover's backdrop is the horizon: dragging ambient 1→20 raises dawn; cue-sheet labels for scenes.
options.case: Fuses cleanly (ambient level maps to dawn) and holds clarity, but loses on audience identification: theatre lighting isn't a headphone owner's world.
options.risk: Leans on gradients, and mode could read as colour alone.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Settings as magnitudes on a chart.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a control panel is not a sky map.
options.kept: One fixed ramp carries hierarchy (the LED ladder everywhere).

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Settings as frames on a rail.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing here is sequential.
options.kept: State as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Arcade CRT
options.case: Fuses poorly: a novelty for a daily tool.
options.kept: Palette law: one colour reserved for one meaning.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.risk: Heavy rendering for a tiny utility.
options.kept: A single active edge line marks the control being changed.

options.label: Pixorama City
options.case: Fuses poorly: noise for a glance tool.
options.kept: One hard grid shared by every element.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A macOS Control Center module: system material, SF Symbols, stock toggles, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Control Center-style tiles for modes, system slider for ambient, a list of settings.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other menu bar utility by design.
